title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. The equivalence 'u descends to 𝔊'^+ ⇔ u normalizes Ker φ' tacitly needs u(Ker φ) = Ker φ, not just ⊆. This is automatic for topologically finitely generated profinite groups (Hopfian property) or finite quotients. That holds for quotients of GL(2,ℤ)^, but it is not stated.

The Remark is syntactically unfinished ('Si on se donne … et qu'on considère … Mais …'), and the marginal hypothesis c_Z ∈ Z^* is added afterwards. The variant Proposition is only announced, not stated.

ideas.what: Criterion for a surjection of profinite groups 𝔊 → 𝔊' to induce compatible maps on the Teichmüller/GT-type groups Z, G, N, M attached to (𝔊,ρ,σ). The criterion is that the relevant automorphisms normalize the kernel ('prolongeable' morphisms).
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of GT-type groups along (characteristic) quotients; descent of automorphisms to quotients; cf. finite-level GT / GT-shadows
ideas.usually_credited_to: Finite-quotient approaches to GT^: Harbater–Schneps, Lochak–Schneps; more recently Dolgushev and collaborators (GT-shadows, ca. 2020s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known; unsure

ideas.what: Extension of φ to a homomorphism of the assembled groups S_0 M^𝔊 → S_0 M^{𝔊'}, compatible with all structure maps Θ.
ideas.modern_name: Functor from prolongeable quotients to GT-like symmetry groups (inverse-system description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in profinite GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara; Lochak–Schneps)

ideas.what: Relative version: fixing a subgroup Z^♮ of the symmetry group and rebuilding G^♮, N^♮, M^♮ from it.
ideas.modern_name: Restricting GT-type group to a subgroup / relative GT groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically sets up functoriality of his 'loop equation' symmetry groups along arbitrary surjections of the profinite group 𝔊. The universal case is GL(2,ℤ)^ with ρ, σ of orders 6 and 4, and the target is its quotients. This is a finite-quotient/inverse-system approach to GT-type groups for the genus-1 (SL2) situation, close in spirit to the recent theory of GT-shadows and 'GT for finite quotients'.
missed.quote: On dira alors que φ est "prolongeable" … On peut alors prolonger φ en (93) φ_M : S_0 G^𝔊_{ρ,σ} → S_0 G^{𝔊'}_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precursor of finite-level GT approaches (Dolgushev et al.) in a GL2/SL2 setting. The content is mostly formal bookkeeping, so it is of limited mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine functoriality section of a long construction: descent of automorphisms to quotients and the induced maps on the assembled groups. It is interesting historically as an early finite-quotient approach to GT-type groups in the GL(2,ℤ)^ setting, but it contains no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: Example line: the image reads 'Supposons Σ^{𝔊'}_{ρ,σ} = Σ^{𝔊' ét}_{ρ,σ}' (étale part of the target), not 'Σ^{𝔊#}'. This fits condition (a) of the Proposition being automatic.
Line 1: 'compatible avec i_{𝔊,G}, i_{Z,G}' (the superscript 'i' in the transcription belongs to i_{𝔊,G}).
Line 2: the crossed-out start is followed by something like 'et qui envoie' / 'applique' N_ρ^𝔊 dans N_ρ^{𝔊'}; the 'obligeant[?]' reading is doubtful.
Corollary line: the image shows 'S_0 G^𝔊_{ρ,σ}' but by the Remark (S_0 M^♮) and the next page (S_0 M^*) it is most likely 'S_0 M_{ρ,σ}'. The handwriting is ambiguous.
Remark: 'Si on se donne un sous-groupe …' rather than 'Si on part qu'on se donne'. The last line probably reads 'Ceci permet … une variante évidente de la proposition'.
Margin: 'Il faut a fortiori supposer que c_Z ∈ Z^*_{ρ,σ}' (probable reading).
